recipes.name: Chocolate Chip Pudding Cookies
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.4 ounce) package instant butterscotch pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Combine the flour and baking soda. Set aside.

Mix the butter, brown sugar, white sugar, pudding mix, and vanilla. Beat until creamy. Add the eggs and mix well. Gradually stir in the flour mixture. Stir in the chocolate chips and the chopped nuts. Drop from teaspoon onto ungreased cookie sheets about 1 inch apart.
Bake at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) for 8 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Chip Pudding Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These cookies change flavors if you change the flavor of the pudding and or the flavor of the chips. They are very cake-like in texture.

review.reviewBody: I have so much fun with this recipe we have renamed it "Surprise Cookies". The possiblilities are as limited as your pudding, chips, and imagination. Variations I have tried are choc. pudding + choc chips, choc pudding + peanut butter chips, lemon pudding + chocolate chips, vanilla pudding + raspberry chips, butterscotch pudding + butterscotch chips (our favorite). Just try whatever crosses your mind! As far as spreading out, I increased the flour to just a little more than 2 1/2 cups. Also, use stick margarine and NOT the soft spread type as they have way too much oil and water.

These are absolutely fantastic!!! I took them to a family BBQ and all cookies were gone quickly! I live at high altitude and added 2 and 1/3 cups of flour. I also baked at 350 for 7 minutes and they came out perfectly!

This another one those OMG recipes, because that's exactly what people are saying when they have one of these cookies. They really are that good. I use french vanilla pudding mix in place of butterscotch and omit the nuts as many people I know do not like them (I love them but am usually not baking for just myself). The trick to keeping these cookies 'melt-in-your-mouth' soft is to pull them out at exactly 8 minutes. I found that even one minute over cooks them too much as they are going to continue to cook once they come out of the oven. They will look undercooked but they're not. Make sure you get an oven thermometer and test your oven's temperature to make sure it's actuate. I discovered over a year ago that mine is running 50 degrees higher than it reads. It was a big reason many of my baked dishes were coming out dry or under-baked in the middle. I tried this once with 'baking' margarine sticks instead of butter...bad idea. The cookies came out very cake-like and 'puffy,' not the look I was going for. Most and chewy is what we want around here!

This recipe is AMAZING as written! I prefer to make larger cookies so I generally yield about 28 cookies per batch. I usually increase the bake time to 10-12 mins. I used chocolate pudding and added dehydrated marshmallow bits & toasted pecan bits along with the chocolate chips! My family devours them & thinks these are DELICIOUS cookies! I’ve been baking a variety of cookies from scratch for MANY years, and (IMHO) these do not taste cheap or store bought as a couple reviewers have mentioned. I use quality ingredients and the results are delicious!

These were amazing! I only baked them for 8 minutes. I also made them only the size of a tablespoon. The batter seemed very strange, but they do turn out great. I used Hershey's dark chocolate pudding and reese's M&M's.

Love these. I used vanilla pudding and used butterscotch and chocolate chips. But the best thing of all I learned something new from a review I read. My cookies for years have always gone flat. I would make sure the butter was not too soft, I would mix by hand so the dough was not over worked you name it and I tried it. So I saw this recipe and thought I am going to try that and as I looked at the reviews someone said to not put the cookie dough on a hot baking sheet because that will cause the cookies to flatten and if you only have one cookie sheet then run it under cool water to cool it down. I am so excited to start making cookies again.

This recipe was almost identical to Amy's Chocolate Chip Cookies, only using all butter and a different pudding flavor. I didn't use all butter only because I was afraid of it spreading, so I used half butter/half margerine. I also used pecans instead of walnuts and I used extra dark chocolate chips. I did chill the dough for about an hour, again because I was afraid of them spreading. Pudding cookies FTW!

I don't follow this exact recipe, but it's the framework for my perfect cookie. I use Godiva white chocolate vanilla bean pudding mix. I also only do max, 2 cups of flour. This helps the cookies rise, but keeps them chewy and skips the cake texture. :) Bake these until the crusts around the outside are JUST golden. I pull them and let them rest, and they are perfectoooo. enjoy!

These were great! I used white chocolate chips and m&m's with vanilla pudding mix. I also added a teaspoon of cinnamon. I rolled them in teaspoon balls and they came out perfectly moist and chewy. They didn't spread out or have a cake-like consistency like others have said. I cooked them for about 8 minutes.

love this recipe! i didnt have nuts or choco chips so i made it with chocolate pudding mix, used 2 1/2 cups of flour and then chilled the cookie mix and then i used the decorating icing recipe (with some strawberry jello for flavor and color) they came out moist and cake like , they were eaten almost immediately..i like how versitile this recipe can be!

I didn’t have butterscotch pudding so used vanilla. Added just a little bit more flour I used almond extract just because I love that taste lolThey turned out amazing. I did have to leave them in the a couple of minutes My 5 year old great granddaughter love them. I had to hide them away. Thank you
So delicious! I add 1/4 cup extra flour to keep them fluffy!
I followed this recipe to a T. So easy. So yum! I am already planning my next batch with peanut butter chips and chocolate pudding!! A keeper for sure!!
Amazing. I like how versatile the cookies are. You can interchange different ingredients and still make wonderful cookies. Thank you for this recipe.
So easy to make taste great. I shared them with my neighbor.
Esasy to make. Love the moistness of the cookie that the oudding adds. Family devoures them. Definitely a keeper.
They turned great.. perfect 😋
I make these all the time, everyone loves them
Best ever.
Very good, turned out perfect!
